nodes.label: 50.1-06-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 06: Gate Identity and Answer Binding Summary

requires.provides: durable::publish_exclusive_durably, remove_durably, replace_durably and rename_to_unique_durably, which every gate file move goes through
workflow::WRITE_LOCK_POLL, WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT and ensure_devflow_dir
supervisor::is_launch_id as pub(crate), the format a gate id shares

provides: gates::GateId, is_gate_id, GateAnswer, OpenedGate, AnswerRead, Claim, CloseReport, ClaimedAnswer, QuarantinedAnswer, GATE_LOCK_WAIT
Gates::open_gate, answer_path, claim_path, answer, reap_answer, read_answer, claim, set_aside_unbound, close, quarantined
GateFile.gate_id and OpenGate.gate_id; write_gate now writes an id and still disposes of nothing
GateError::InvalidGateId, GateIdMismatch, GateClosedAfterPublish, GateLockTimeout, PublishedUnconfirmed
The per-phase gate lock .devflow/.gates-NN.lock, and the events gate_answer_quarantined and gate_claimed_answer_removed
durable::rename_to_unique_durably has its first non-test caller; its three dead-code expectations are gone

patterns: A writer publishes outside the gate lock and checks the gate file under it on both sides of the publish
Only absence reads as absent: any other read failure stays an error and moves nothing
A kill-point fixture runs in a child that exits with a named code at a private hook; the parent asserts the code before reading anything

key-decisions: A claimed body that never bound to its gate is set aside, not deleted, and reported with answer None: a claim does not license deleting it (D-05)
GateClosedAfterPublish's message says the answer was set aside unless its waiter had already consumed it, because the re-check cannot tell those apart
A lone legacy NN-{stage}.ack.json is removed by the stage disposal: it holds no decision, and leaving it would keep the phase listed by phases_on_disk
From answer, Io and Json can come from either side of the publish, and GateError's doc says so
patterns-established: Every answer is set aside through the private set_aside, so no move can skip the event or the no-replace name
Stage files are processed in name order, so reports and kill-point fixtures are deterministic

coverage.description: A gate has a fresh id, an answer is keyed by it and names it, and a claim is first-wins
An id-less, wrong-gate or hostile answer is set aside under a name no other process can take, and a valid answer is then accepted (V-15, V-16, R-09, R-11)
A late writer cannot decide the next gate, and a published answer is never reported as nothing changed (V-18, R2-04)
A closed or replaced gate can never be claimed again (R-08)
A removed claim is always reported, and a close killed mid-disposal leaves the gate file and the unremoved pair (R-02, R2-05)
The gate lock is bounded and ordered after the state write lock (D-08 ruling, V-80, V-81); direct workflow paths only, an indirect path rests on review
Open and close dispose of the stage, status can list what was set aside, reap_answer can only reject, and list_open hides a gate only for its own answer
The unkeyed API behaves as before for the CLI until 50.1-13/-14 move off it

requires.provides: durable::fsync_dir and the cfg(test) recorder durable::take_synced, which the sidecar publish and its test use

provides: liveness::Hold, Held, probe: an exclusive flock on a 0600 per-launch file, probed live, abandoned or missing with no pid read
liveness::Hold::take publishes a hold's name only once it is held (R-06), by a no-replace hard link from a locked temp
liveness::pass_to_child (crate-private) and adopt_inherited: hand the lock to a child at fd 3, and take it over on the supervisor side
liveness::live_holder, launch_liveness_path, remove_orphan_hold_temps, HOLD_TEMP_SUFFIX, INHERITED_FD
liveness::write_identity_record (crate-private): the one positional writer of a hold's record (R-01)
liveness::take_with_hook and TakeStep (crate-private; take_with_hook is cfg(test)): pause a take at each step
supervisor::is_launch_id is pub(crate); write_sidecar fsyncs its directory after the link

patterns: A test that moves descriptors by number, or reads a lock right after its release, runs in its own process (in_own_process), with no other test's fork holding a duplicate
A test of a file mode clears the umask in its own process, because a host umask of 0077 narrows a wrong mode into the right one

key-decisions: The fixture's hold_at_fd_3 returns a hold that already is at fd 3. With fd 3 freed, the take's own temp open lands there, so the plan's fcntl(raw, F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC, 3) would return another number
remove_orphan_hold_temps returns only the paths it removed: a NotFound from remove_file is tolerated and not listed
pass_to_child carries expect(dead_code) until its first production caller in 50.1-07
patterns-established: Every hold is created through Hold::take, and released only by dropping it
A hold's identity record is written only by write_identity_record

coverage.description: A child inherits a liveness hold at fd 3 and keeps it after the parent drops its copy, whether or not the descriptor already was fd 3; a dup2-only variant loses it (control)
A probe reads live, abandoned or missing from the lock alone; a probe in flight neither reads live nor fails a take; a real holder still reads live and refuses a second taker
No code unlocks a hold; unlock on a duplicate is shown releasing the inherited lock
Adoption marks the descriptor close-on-exec and records the adopter; a record rewritten on an advanced shared offset has no NUL hole (cursor-write control reads InvalidData); a torn record is refused
A hold's name is never visible unheld while its creator lives, with a sweep in each gap of the take; the create-then-lock control ends with a held hold reading Missing
An orphaned hold temp is removed only when it is unheld and its creator is gone; a final name, a foreign shape or a live creator's temp is kept
The sidecar publish fsyncs its directory after the link, and a refused second write records no fsync
launch_liveness_path refuses a launch id is_launch_id rejects

nodes.label: 50.1-08-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 08: Gate Waiter Registration and the Binding Wait Summary

requires.provides: liveness::{Hold, probe, Held, live_holder, HOLD_TEMP_SUFFIX} and the no-replace Hold::take, plus the cfg(test) take_with_hook and TakeStep
GateId, open_gate, answer, answer_with_hook, read_answer, set_aside_unbound, close, claim and the gate lock

provides: Gates::{waiter_path, register_waiter, waiter_status, live_waiter_holders, open_registered, await_answer}
WaiterRegistration (finish), WaiterStatus { Live, Absent }, AwaitOutcome { Answered, Unbound { reason }, TimedOut, Cancelled }, which stays exhaustive
backoff_wait: the one wait loop, reading at 1 s doubling to 60 s and at the timeout, with cancel checked first and at least once a second
Test builds only: Gates::preanswer_path, consume_preanswer, the answer-publish hook slot
test_support::{preanswer_gate, answer_open_gate, gate_answer_files, with_answer_before_publish}
Transition bridge, deleted in 50.1-15: the unkeyed polls read the live keyed answer, and unkeyed cleanup removes keyed files and abandoned waiter files

patterns: A gate's waiter is a held flock taken before the gate file is published
A wait reads, and a caller moves: await_answer returns an unbound body untouched
A hook seam that must run in a release-shaped path sits on an ungated private fn that is the public fn's whole body; only the control is cfg(test)

key-decisions: The timeout is a read boundary, which the plan's loop did not have, so an answer landing in the last backoff gap is an answer, not a timeout
Gates::current_gate_id is pub(crate), so test_support::answer_open_gate does not repeat the gate-file parse
test_support::preanswer_gate returns nothing and panics on failure, as the plan's signature shows and 50.1-12's call sites use it
patterns-established: A test that reads a lock right after its release runs in a child process of its own, because another test's fork can hold a duplicate descriptor under cargo test

coverage.description: A waiter reads live exactly while it holds its registration, and a crashed waiter reads absent; registration needs no supervisor socket, though only in-process registration was exercised (D-04, T-50.1-27)
A gate file is never visible before its waiter's registration, by the code a release build ships (V-35, T-50.1-103)
The wait moves no file and hands an unbound answer back, and a waiter whose gate was replaced touches nothing (R-09, V-15 waiter half, T-50.1-119)
Only an abandoned registration is removed by anyone but its owner, and a take in flight is not a gate file (R-06, T-50.1-120, T-50.1-121)
The wait backs off between reads, still cancels within about a second, and lets a stop beat an answer (999.166 items 4 and 7 core half, V-25, T-50.1-28, T-50.1-29)
A test-only pre-answer and answer-publish hook, with their helpers; the pre-answer half in gates.rs is held by a source scan with planted controls (V-36, T-50.1-30, T-50.1-104)
The CLI keeps working unchanged on the transition bridge (T-50.1-31)

requires.provides: workflow::{update_state_with_within, WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT, WorkflowError::WriteLockTimeout}
Gates::{claim_path, claim}, GateError::{GateLockTimeout, PublishedUnconfirmed}, gates::GATE_LOCK_WAIT
Gates::{waiter_status, register_waiter, live_waiter_holders}, WaiterStatus
stop's pending branch and clear_abandoned_reservation
stop_via_holder, wait_for_holder_release, missing_state_line, liveness::phase_holder_path

provides: waiter_is_live reads only the registration; gate respond, sweep, stop and doctor decide from it
persist_stopped_state(root, phase, signal_sent, known_launches): bounded by WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT, refuses a launch no arm addressed
SocketStop::Ended { launch_id } and SocketStop::NoLiveSocket { gone }; LocatedSocket.launch_id
stop_via_gate declines a claimed gate, falls through on GateLockTimeout, treats PublishedUnconfirmed as answered
registry_reachable_pids from held liveness, registration and holder files
ship_override and persist_stopped_state take no per-phase lock

patterns: stop keeps one list of launches its arms addressed; no state read seeds it, and the fresh read under the write lock decides
A test reading a released flock polls with a bound, or removes the file through finish()

key-decisions: stop_via_gate returns Option<AnsweredGate>: once no not-answered path carries a gate, the old bool was redundant
AnsweredGate stays a tuple (stage, gate id, run's launch id); only the launch id is read in production, and a struct's unread fields would fail clippy
A held gate lock or an unconfirmed publish ends gate sweep through CliError::Gate, which also skips a requested stray pass in that run
patterns-established: An e2e test pins a line stop prints, since a unit test cannot see stdout

coverage.description: gate approve|reject answers a registered waiter, refuses when none is registered even beside a live lock record, and stores a Ship answer
A held gate lock ends a writer within its bound with nothing written; stop falls through; an unconfirmed publish is answered for stop and an error for the writers
stop's state write is bounded: a stopped write-lock holder ends it within 10-12 s, named, with the state byte-identical
stop never marks stopped beside a launch none of its arms ended, answered, cleared or found not live
stop never answers a claimed gate and reaches the holder past it
Sweep, stop and doctor read the registration; the stray safety set is the holders of held files

nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 24: `stop` says what actually happened Summary

requires.provides: `LiveAgent`, `live_phase_agent`, `orphaned_agent_line`, and `status`'s half of D-19
`stop_via_holder`'s no-holder branch

provides: `ShutdownStopped.group_signalled` and `ShutdownOutcome::Stopped.group_signalled`, true only when a stop signal actually went out
`ShutdownOutcome::AcceptedPending { owner }` for a stop accepted with no final line within the wait
`stop` lines that name the safe point, the pending stop, or the orphaned agent
`run_monitor` writes 143 to the exit file after a safe-point stop (D-16)

patterns: A reply states a fact recorded where the action happened, so a refused signal is not reported as sent

key-decisions: The pending line names `devflow status`, because `devflow status --phase N` as the plan wrote it does not exist
`group_signalled` is recorded where the signal is sent, and a stop forwarded to a next or successor supervisor carries that supervisor's answer
A superseded supervisor and a handed-off run do not write 143
patterns-established: An accepted stop is a distinct outcome: `stop_pending_launch` returns on it, so it never asks the same supervisor again in a loop

coverage.description: `stop`'s success line says "agent group ended" only when a group was signalled, and otherwise names the safe point and says nothing was signalled
After a safe-point stop the exit file records 143, the reply's code, and a resumed run is judged on its own exit code
A stop the supervisor accepted with no final line in time reads as pending, is recorded `stopped`, and never reads "nothing was signalled or recorded"
With no supervisor, pending launch or holder and the phase's agent alive, `stop` names the pid and the manual kill, signals nothing, writes nothing and exits non-zero

nodes.label: 50.1-29-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 29: Phase Holder and Foreground Stop Summary

requires.provides: liveness::{Hold, probe, live_holder, write_identity_record, try_lock_past_probes}
reserve_launch, hold_reservation, abandon_reservation, launch_test_hold
stop's pending branch and its bounded wait for a socket
no long advance lock, the gap this plan's live-supervisor refusal closes

provides: liveness::{phase_holder_path, claim_phase_holder, HolderError, install_holder_stop_handler, holder_stop_signal}
commands::{claim_foreground_holder, stop_via_holder, refuse_advance_over_a_live_supervisor, refuse_ship_over_a_live_supervisor}
pipeline_launch::{advance_command, HOLDER_STOP_REASON, safe_point_stop_reason}
advance_stopped gains source: supervisor | foreground_holder
launch_test_hold point holder_claimed

patterns: A foreground process claims .devflow/.holder-NN through one function, with the stop handler installed first
A signal to a foreground holder sets a flag read at safe points, never an interruption
signal_sent means one fact: stop_via_holder signalled a foreground holder

key-decisions: When a signalled launcher exits but its launch's liveness lock is still held, a supervisor it spawned holds it, so stop refuses and writes nothing. The plan named only the abandoned outcome
stop_pending_launch returns a PendingStop enum, so stop_in can tell a socket stop (signal_sent false) from a signalled launcher (true)
The pending branch probes the holder file before calling stop_via_holder, so it does not print 'nothing is running' just before refusing over a live reservation
The refusal over a socket directory that cannot be listed says 'may have a live supervisor', since nothing was seen
patterns-established: A test that must read a released flock runs in its own child process, as in_own_hermetic_process does
A test can read a claim file before an abort removes it, by parking the consumer on ClaimProbe

coverage.description: A hand-run advance holds the phase; stop signals it after the identity check; it catches the signal and stops at safe point 1
A holder turns SIGTERM and SIGINT into a flag; a foreground gate wait ends at safe point 4; no-handler controls die by the signal
start, resume, ship and advance refuse over a held phase before any write; a refused start or resume reserves nothing
A hand-run advance and devflow ship refuse beside a live recorded or pending supervisor, with GONE controls that reach the advance and the claim
stop reaches a start before its spawn; the launcher stops at safe point 2 and gives its reservation back; both ends of the release wait are pinned
Recycled, start-time-less, unreadable and unheld records signal nothing, and a socket stop is never reported as a signalled holder

requires.provides: pipeline_launch::commit and the already-migrated gate, launch and ceiling-reset writes
workflow::update_state, update_state_with and the Existing enum

provides: No production save_state reference in either crate, enforced by two source scans with planted controls
Outcome handlers, run_preflight and persist_stopped_state write only their own fields, on the state re-read under the write lock
commands::create_run_state: start's fresh run written under the write lock, for 50.1-16 to turn into a check-and-reserve
workflow::save_state compiled only for tests and the test-support feature (R-10)
test_support::state_on_disk_at_gate: reads the file while a handler is held at its gate, because an abort clears it

patterns: A decision on a counter reads the committed copy: commit first, then compare, so no value is projected from the caller's copy
Work a closure may not do (git, plan-file scan, println) runs outside it: the result goes in, or the closure's value comes out

key-decisions: The infra ceiling is read after the commit on the rate-limit and ambiguous paths, so both now call gate_or_abort_infra rather than handle_infra_outcome at the ceiling
The checkpoint-set recorder split in two: a scan outside the lock, and a fill on the re-read state that applies the only-from-Pending rule again
persist_stopped_state uses the blocking update_state_with as the plan says; 50.1-20 (R-03) moves it to the bounded form
The core scan exempts only the definition line; the CLI scan has no exemption, because the CLI defines no save_state
patterns-established: state_on_disk_at_gate: assert on-disk fields of a handler whose gate answer would clear the file

coverage.description: Validate and infra outcomes commit their counters on the re-read state and keep a concurrent field
run_preflight's retry counter, stop's reason and start's create all go through the write lock
A production save_state reference in either crate fails the suite (V-11)
save_state is absent from the default-feature devflow-core API and present for every test target (R-10)

verification.ref: cargo build -p devflow-core && cargo build -p devflow && cargo build --workspace --all-targets
cargo semver-checks check-release -p devflow-core --default-features --baseline-rev cf1a93f reports exactly function_missing: workflow::save_state

coverage.description: No closure assigns a whole State copy except start's create, and the scans allowlist no production file
coverage.rationale: The plan marks both prohibitions as judgment. A scan of these sites finds no `*s =` or `*state =`, and the scans' only exclusions are `mod tests`, whole-line comments, test_support.rs and core's definition line. The closure bodies were read by the executor only, with no independent review.

requires.provides: pending_supervisor, reserve_launch, pending_live_socket, DEVFLOW_TEST_AGENT_SPAWN_HOLD
the handoff's pending record, end_unpublished at safe point 3
update_state_with_within, write_lock_status, WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT, WriteLockTimeout

provides: PhaseLiveness::LaunchPending { launch_id, published } (label launch_pending), read through the launch guard's own predicate
stop_in handles pending_supervisor: socket shutdown, bounded publish wait (PENDING_PUBLISH_WAIT), abandoned-reservation clear on the bounded write
doctor finding and doctor --json reconciliation[].supervisor.pending (null or {launch_id, liveness})
D-19 helpers for 50.1-24: LiveAgent, live_phase_agent, orphaned_agent_line, status_hints; PhaseFacts.live_agent
R-03 helpers: write_lock_line, check_write_lock; PhaseFacts.write_lock

patterns: Status and doctor share one predicate with the launch guard, so they cannot disagree about a pending supervisor

key-decisions: A stopped phase whose supervisor is GONE or unrecorded now gets a devflow resume hint. Criterion 2's control and the plan's e2e need it, because stop marks the phase stopped and status previously said nothing there
An abandoned reservation with no record reads GONE rather than not launched, so resume is suggested in the no-record case too
A live liveness lock beats a STALE pending socket: stop waits rather than run the backstop, which is for a supervisor that is gone
After the pending step stop looks at the recorded socket again, because a launch promoted during the wait ends the pending record and not the supervisor

A doctor repair that would name resume names stop while a pending supervisor lives, 'wait for its live supervisor, or devflow stop' while an ALIVE one does, and the manual kill beside an orphaned agent
live_phase_agent never returns pid 0 or 1, because the caller prints it as a process group to signal

coverage.description: V-07, V-08: status names only devflow stop while a pending supervisor lives, with a GONE record or none, and names devflow resume once its lock is released, noting the abandoned reservation
stop ends a pending supervisor through its socket, published or still unpublished when stop starts, for rows A7 and C4, names no resume, and status suggests resume afterwards

V-09 and R-03: stop clears an abandoned reservation with a report; a held lock with no socket ends non-zero after the wait with nothing written; a held write lock ends the clear within the bound, naming the holder
doctor names a pending launch and stop, in text and JSON, over a GONE and a STALE record; no doctor repair names resume while a supervisor or orphaned agent lives
D-19 and R-03 in status and doctor: an orphaned agent is named with its manual kill, with a dead-agent control; a held write lock is named without waiting, with a released control

requires.provides: update_owned_state, ownership, NotOwner, write_lock_status, WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT
the gate lock and its two lock-order pins, Gates::claim, set_aside_unbound
waiter registration on every gate wait, the facts the rewritten tests wait on
reservations and the interim promotion wait this plan removes
the handoff's pending record

provides: workflow::while_owner and workflow::clear_state_if_owned
monitor::Promotion, StageSpec.promotion_wait, StageRun.promotion, StageRun.agent_group_end, the promotion-watch thread
Supervisor::end_agent_group, AgentGroupEnd, StopSource::Ownership, end_group_while_running (R-13's rule)
CLI: fenced, close_gate, clear_run_state, ensure_still_recorded, PROMOTION_WAIT_RELEASE, PROMOTION_WAIT, event supervisor_superseded
#[cfg(test)] hold points after_claim and after_commit in run_gate_with_timeout, for 50.1-23

patterns: A gate side effect shares one hold of the state write lock with its ownership check, through fenced
A supervisor decides whether it owns the run beside its agent, from the moment it serves
A process group is signalled by number only while its leader is unreaped

key-decisions: wait_while_launch_is_pending is removed with its three tests. The promotion watch replaces its ordering, and it no longer advances when the wait expires
A supervisor whose launcher died no longer reaches its next handoff to be refused there: it never advances, and ends at the deadline
A stop ends the promotion wait early. Waiting out the deadline after a stop would delay the final stopped line past safe point 3's bound
A superseded supervisor starts no checkout hook: ensure_still_recorded runs before each batch. The plan's fence covered state and gates, and the RED run showed a superseded supervisor still merging

publish_record's second write moves to save_successor_stop, an owned write for the successor, so the first save can be fenced to the engaged supervisor without telling the two saves apart by state.stopped
abort returns NotOwner before it deregisters the phase or emits workflow_aborted, because a superseded supervisor ends nothing

coverage.description: Every state write in a supervisor's advance is owner-fenced, a hand-run advance stays unfenced, and a state clear is fenced
R-09: each gate side effect shares one write-lock hold with its ownership check; a superseded waiter leaves the current gate's files byte-identical
V-23: a superseded supervisor writes nothing, claims nothing, spawns nothing, promotes nothing, starts no hook, emits one event and exits; the recorded one writes normally
V-24: a fast agent waits for its launcher's promotion, then advances; the wait is unit-tested for each verdict
V-27, R-12: an orphan ends its still-running agent's whole group at the deadline and writes nothing; one whose agent already exited stops short of its handoff; a promoted supervisor keeps its agent
R-13: no group is signalled by number after its leader is reaped; a running agent's group is ended
D-08: advance holds no long lock, and every test that observed it now waits on the gate's registration or the write lock

nodes.label: 50.1-04-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 04: State Write Lock and Owner Fence Summary

requires.provides: durable::replace_durably and remove_durably, which every write and clear here goes through

provides: workflow::update_state, update_state_with and Existing: lock, re-read, apply, durable write, release
workflow::update_owned_state, ownership, Ownership and WorkflowError::NotOwner: the core half of the owner fence (D-03)

workflow::update_state_with_within, clear_state_within, write_lock_status, WriteLockStatus, WRITE_LOCK_POLL, WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT and WorkflowError::WriteLockTimeout: bounded acquisition that names the holder (R-03)
state::PendingSupervisor and State.pending_supervisor (D-01 shape)
workflow::write_lock_is_free and DEVFLOW_TEST_SKIP_WRITE_LOCK: test support for 50.1-16's control

patterns: A test that asserts a just-released flock is free polls for up to 2 s, because under cargo test another thread's fork keeps a duplicate of the descriptor until its exec. A real leak outlasts the poll
A test child holding a lock signals readiness by creating a file from inside the closure, so the parent knows the right test holds the lock before it sends SIGSTOP

key-decisions: A blocked flock retries EINTR. std's File::lock does not (measured: the write failed with Interrupted without the retry). DevFlow's own stop handler sets SA_RESTART, so only a library host's handler reaches this arm today
clear_state in a project with no .devflow directory returns without taking the lock, so it does not create .devflow in a project DevFlow has not touched
WriteLockTimeout.waited holds the wait the call allowed, not a measured elapsed time, so the message reads 500ms rather than 500.336143ms
Existing keeps Loaded(State) as the plan specifies, under an allow for clippy::large_enum_variant: it is passed by value to one closure and consumed there
patterns-established: Workflow writers use the blocking form; a verb that diagnoses a wedge (stop, recover, status, doctor) uses the bounded form or write_lock_status

coverage.description: update_state re-reads under a short write lock, so a change made between a caller's load and its update survives; a stale copy saved whole loses it (control)
clear_state takes the same lock, and creates nothing in a project with no .devflow directory
The write lock is not inherited by a close-on-exec child (control: a child with close-on-exec cleared keeps it), and a signal without SA_RESTART does not fail a blocked write

A bounded write or clear returns by its deadline against a SIGSTOPped holder, runs no closure, writes nothing and names the holder; a dead or absent record reads as unknown; write_lock_status reads free, held and the recorded holder without creating a file
update_state_with creates a missing state only when asked, reports an unloadable one untouched, and refuses a state for another phase
The test-only seam takes no lock, and its read is allowlisted (control: removing the entry fails doc_check)
State.pending_supervisor sits beside State.supervisor and round-trips; an older file without the key parses as None
ownership tells recorded, pending and superseded apart; update_owned_state refuses before its closure and writes nothing

nodes.label: 50.1-21-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 21: Recover decides liveness without a lock Summary

requires.provides: stop, sweep, doctor and strays on registrations, so nothing outside recover and tests still used the per-phase lock
remove_gate_files as a per-stage close loop, which this plan replaces

provides: recover::phase_may_be_live: recorded socket, pending socket and lock, held waiters, D-17 holder; fail closed
workflow::clear_state_if and Cleared<A>: decide, remove and an after-clear step under one write-lock hold, optionally bounded
Gates::close_phase and close_phase_with_partial_result: every stage under one gate-lock acquisition
recover --clean sweeps abandoned supervisor-*.live, *.waiter and orphan *.hold-tmp, and lists set-aside answers
The per-phase pid-lock API is deleted from devflow-core

patterns: A destructive repair decides inside clear_state_if, on the read it hands the closure, and every path it deletes by phase goes inside the same hold
A control that needs a just-released flock to read free retries the idempotent call with a bound

key-decisions: A phase kept as live by the explicit clean is reported through report.fail, so the CLI exits non-zero without a new public field on PhaseCleanReport
The orphan gate pass and the explicit clean of a missing or unparsable state also check the waiter and holder files, because the lock they replace refused whatever the state said
The orphan gate and cron passes keep an unlocked state_path exists check before their locked decision. It can only keep, and it spares a kept phase two more 10 s waits on a held lock
RecoverError::Lock stays, unconstructed: removing it is a break no 50.1 plan declared. Logged for 50.1-28
lock.rs keeps a private HolderClass for the checkout lock's reclaim in place of the public HolderStatus
patterns-established: clear_state_if's two closures must not take the write lock; a gate wait inside is the bounded one the D-08 ruling allows

coverage.description: recover --clean without --phase keeps a stale phase whose supervisor, pending supervisor, gate waiter or foreground holder may be live, naming why and devflow stop
The decision and the removals share one write-lock hold on a fresh read, so a run reserved after the listing keeps its state, gate files and cron record
One decision waits at most two socket probes and one gate wait, and a held write lock ends an explicit clean within the bound, naming its holder
Inspect and explicit clean ask the processes, not a lock file; the CLI prints the live reason, removed markers and set-aside answers

verification.ref: cargo nextest run -p devflow --test recover_clean_e2e --no-tests=fail (15 passed)

coverage.description: Abandoned markers are swept without an age bound, including inside a paused take, and the three lock files are never touched
The per-phase pid-lock API is gone and a leftover lock-NN is removed as stale

verification.ref: cargo nextest run -p devflow --test gate_wedge_e2e --no-tests=fail (5 passed)

nodes.label: 51-06-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 51 Plan 06: Failover Hop Hardening Summary

requires.provides: 51-01: hand_off_agent, failover_target, fail_over_on_rate_limit, the RateLimited arm and the 50-13 handoff harness with a second stub; 51-04: State.fallback_agent set by --fallback-agent

provides: hand_off_agent's single commit clears state.canary and state.session_id (D-04)
agent_handoff event keys tree_dirty (bool or null) and commit_count (u32 or null) (D-10, D-08)
agent_handoff_relaunch_failed event (stage, from_agent, to_agent, reason)
fail_over_on_rate_limit routes a non-NotOwner relaunch error to handle_infra_outcome (R2-D1) and returns NotOwner unchanged
private FailoverRelaunchGuard and in_failover_relaunch(), read by refuse_launch and record_failed_launch
#[cfg(test)] hold point after_failover_commit
eight tests and one scan clause

patterns: Per-thread RAII flag (FailoverRelaunchGuard) beside ENGAGED_ADVANCE/HELD_RESERVATION that narrows WR-04's record clear to non-failover launches
Source-scan clause that matches only a line's code part (cut at the first // outside a string literal)

key-decisions: A failover relaunch that fails after the handoff commit emits agent_handoff_relaunch_failed and calls handle_infra_outcome (one infra bump, then the never-silent gate or the abort at the ceiling); FailoverRelaunchGuard keeps the supervisor record through that relaunch only, so those writes stay owned under the Phase 50 D-03 fence
agent_handoff_relaunch_failed carries the full error text; the gate context starts 'the handoff to <fallback> could not relaunch the <stage> stage:' so truncation keeps the fallback's name
Tree fields are measured before the handoff commit at state.worktree_path or project_root; null means git could not answer, never a made-up value
patterns-established: A relaunch that may keep the supervisor record is marked by an RAII guard scoped to one launch_stage call and pinned to one call site by a source scan

coverage.description: The handoff commit clears the recorded canary and session id, so a fallback whose own canary reads Absent is refused after one canary run; control: without the handoff the recorded Confirmed admits it with zero runs
agent_handoff records tree_dirty and commit_count; an untracked file survives the handoff
A zero-commit Code rate limit still hands off through advance, with commit_count 0 and tree_dirty false
Boundaries at Code: one below the infra ceiling a hop charges nothing (no-fallback control aborts); a consumed or equal fallback takes the cron arm; an Ambiguous outcome re-drives without handing off
Inside a real supervisor, a relaunch refused after the handoff commit emits agent_handoff_relaunch_failed and ends at the Code gate opened by the recorded supervisor; no cron arm, no supersession
A supervisor replaced before its failover relaunch's first owned write writes nothing; the guard is engaged only in fail_over_on_rate_limit

nodes.label: 50.1-01-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 01: Durable File Helpers Summary

provides: crates/devflow-core/src/durable.rs: replace_durably, publish_exclusive_durably, Publication, remove_durably, rename_durably, rename_to_unique_durably, create_dir_all_durably, fsync_dir
#[cfg(test)] Synced and take_synced: a per-thread ordered fsync recorder for later plans' tests
durable::tests::state_and_gate_modules_mutate_files_only_through_the_durable_helpers: the D-09 source scan

patterns: Every file mutation in workflow.rs and gates.rs goes through a durable.rs helper, enforced by a text scan with planted controls
Ordered thread-local fsync recorder: tests assert which fsyncs happened and in what order

key-decisions: Kept the path.exists() guards in clear_state and Gates::cleanup rather than relying on remove_durably's NotFound: without them a state or gate path under a parent that is not a directory would change from a skip to an error, and this plan must not change what these functions decide
create_dir_all_durably errors on a file in the way (AlreadyExists and not a directory), matching std::fs::create_dir_all, instead of syncing the parent and returning success
publish_exclusive_durably fsyncs the directory first and reports a failed temp removal after, keeping the old writer's behaviour of returning an error on a failed cleanup after a successful publish
patterns-established: A helper with no caller yet carries cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = ...)), so the first caller's clippy run forces the attribute's removal

coverage.description: State saves and gate request/ack writes fsync a temp file, rename it, then fsync the directory, in that order
A gate response is published by fsync, hard link, directory fsync, never by rename; a second publisher still gets AlreadyResponded
clear_state and gate cleanup unlink then fsync the directory; a missing file reads as not removed
Directory creation fsyncs the parent on every return, including a directory another process made (R2-08); the .gitignore marker stays create_new with no temp (R-15)
rename_to_unique_durably moves a file to a new name by a no-replace hard link and never overwrites an existing name (R-11); 50.1-06 adds its first caller
A source scan fails on a direct fs::write, rename, hard_link or remove_file in the non-test code of workflow.rs or gates.rs

nodes.label: 50.1-16-SUMMARY.md
nodes.community_name: Phase 50.1 Plan 16: Record the Supervisor Before Spawn Summary

requires.provides: monitor::Reservation, spawn_monitor(&reservation), the __monitor process's inherited liveness lock
workflow::update_state_with, Existing, DEVFLOW_TEST_SKIP_WRITE_LOCK
Gate waits register before they publish, which gate_wedge_e2e now asserts in place of the lock

provides: commands::reserve_launch: the live-run guard and the pending_supervisor write in one write-lock closure
start and resume with no long per-phase lock
A guard that reads pending_supervisor: a held lock is live, an unheld or missing one is abandoned and cleared
pipeline_launch::{hold_reservation, take_held_reservation, abandon_reservation, launch_test_hold}; publish_record promotes; record_failed_launch clears
monitor::Reservation::{for_phase, discard}; DEVFLOW_TEST_AGENT_SPAWN_HOLD=<stage>:<path>

patterns: A launcher's reservation lives in a thread-local slot between the top of start/resume and the spawn, so every path between them keeps its signature and one wrapper gives it back

key-decisions: A fast agent's advance waits (bounded, 15 s) while its launch is only pending. The long lock used to order that advance against the launcher's publish, and without it the publish could overwrite the next stage's record. 50.1-19's promotion watch replaces this
The pending half lives in possibly_live_sockets, so recover --clean also refuses over a live pending supervisor. Without it, clean would delete a live launch's state now that no lock contends
An abandoned liveness file is removed only at the path its launch id derives to and only while it probes abandoned, because the recorded path comes from a state file
A resume refused over a pending supervisor closes with `devflow status --phase N` and omits the agent paragraph, since both of its usual lines name `devflow resume`

coverage.description: start names its supervisor before it exists, the supervisor publishes under that id, and the publish save promotes it
A start that fails after reserving gives the reservation back: no state it created, an earlier run's state byte-identical, no liveness file

V-01: with the launcher SIGKILLed and its supervisor held before its agent spawn, a second start and a second resume refuse, name devflow stop --phase N and the pending id, say nothing of devflow resume, and write nothing
V-03 and V-04: an abandoned reservation blocks nothing and is reported; a live agent named by the pid file still refuses
V-05: check-and-reserve is one atomic step, with a control that removes the write lock
start and resume hold no long lock; the suites premised on it assert the reservation and the registered waiter
The 50.1-07 carry-overs: the launcher's drop order is pinned, and a real-binary supervisor's lock is read
A fast agent's advance waits for its promotion, within a bound

truths: D-09 replace: `save_state` (through `write_state_atomic`) and `gates.rs`'s request/ack writer fsync the temp file, rename it over the target, then fsync the directory; `durable::tests::replace_fsyncs_the_file_and_its_directory` records exactly `[File(temp), Dir(parent)]` in that order

D-09 exclusive publish: a gate response is published by fsync-temp, hard-link, directory fsync, and never falls back to rename; a second publisher gets `AlreadyExists`, which `gates.rs` still maps to `GateError::AlreadyResponded` (Phase 48 D-04 first answer wins)
D-09 remove: `clear_state` and gate cleanup unlink, then fsync the directory; a missing file reads as not removed, not as an error

D-09 / Pitfall 11: a `.devflow/` or `.devflow/gates/` directory created on first write is made durable by fsyncing its parent; the `.devflow/.gitignore` marker keeps today's `create_new` + `AlreadyExists → Ok(())` (first creator wins, an existing file of any content is left untouched), so a steady-state call — every state write after the first — creates no temp file (R-15; `workflow::tests::ensure_devflow_dir_steady_state_creates_no_temp_and_fsyncs_only_the_parent`, whose in-test control shows the excl

R2-08 (round-2 review, codex 8): a directory that already exists may have been made by another process that has not yet fsynced its parent, so `create_dir_all_durably` fsyncs the parent of its last component on every successful return — after creating it, after a racing creator's `AlreadyExists`, and when it existed at entry — and `ensure_devflow_dir` applies the same rule to the `.devflow` component when it is given a directory below it (`.devflow/gates`), so no state or gate writer returns success on

D-05 support (R-11): `durable::rename_to_unique_durably(from, dir, stem, suffix)` moves a file to a NEW name `{stem}.{pid}.{seq}{suffix}` in `dir` by a no-replace `hard_link` (`AlreadyExists` → the next `seq`, never an overwrite), then removes the source and fsyncs the directory; the pid component makes names from different processes distinct and the retry makes a reused pid with a restarted counter safe — `durable::tests::a_unique_rename_never_replaces_an_existing_name`, whose in-test control shows `rename

D-09 source scan (criterion 3): `durable::tests::state_and_gate_modules_mutate_files_only_through_the_durable_helpers` fails on any `fs::write(`, `rename(`, `hard_link(` or `remove_file(` in the non-test code of `workflow.rs` or `gates.rs`, and a planted `std::fs::rename` yields exactly its violation

R-16 exemption, chosen not overlooked: the advisory coordination files of this phase — `supervisor-<id>.live` (50.1-05/-07), `NN-{stage}.{gate_id}.waiter` (50.1-08), `.devflow/.holder-NN` (50.1-29), the write lock `.devflow/.state-NN.lock` (50.1-04), a hold's `*.hold-tmp` temp (50.1-05) and `.devflow/.gitignore` — are outside D-09's three operations and outside this scan's scope (`workflow.rs`, `gates.rs`). Why: none of them holds a state or gate record; a held `flock`, not their bytes

D-11 staging: until 50.1-09 deletes it, `migrate_legacy_state`'s rename and remove also go through `rename_durably`/`remove_durably`, so the scan holds from this plan on; this plan does not change what the migration does

truths: D-04: `Gates::open_gate` writes a fresh 16-hex gate id into the gate file and returns it; every gate a process opens has a new id, so phase and stage become the gate's location and the gate id its identity

D-05: an answer is stored keyed by gate id (`NN-{stage}.{gate_id}.response.json`) and its body carries the same `gate_id`; `Gates::answer` and `Gates::reap_answer` take the gate id the writer observed, refuse when the gate file names another id (`GateError::GateIdMismatch`) and re-check after publishing (`GateError::GateClosedAfterPublish`), so a decision about G1 cannot be relabelled onto G2; before publishing, a writer moves an answer in its own gate's slot that does not bind to that gate aside (so a

D-05: an answer with a missing gate id, an unparsable body, another gate's id, or a legacy unkeyed name is renamed to a quarantine name beside it (`NN-{stage}.{gate_id|noid}.{secs}.{pid}.{seq}.quarantined.json`, published by `durable::rename_to_unique_durably`'s no-replace hard link, so two processes setting answers aside in the same second never overwrite each other — R-11, `gates::tests::two_processes_quarantining_in_one_second_keep_both_answers`), logged, and recorded as a `gate_answer_quaranti

R-09: no gate function that a reader or a waiter calls mutates another gate's files. `read_answer` and `list_open` only read; `Gates::set_aside_unbound(root, phase, stage, &G)` and `Gates::answer` move at most the one file in G's own slot, and only while the gate file names G (checked under the gate lock); the stage-wide disposal runs only inside `open_gate` and `close`

R-08: a closed or replaced gate never becomes claimable again. `Gates::claim` publishes its ack only while, under the phase's gate lock, the gate file still names the claimed id (gate file absent → `GateError::NoOpenGate`; another id → `GateError::GateIdMismatch`; nothing is published either way); `open_gate` and `close` replace or remove the gate file under the same lock, and gate ids are never reused — `gates::tests::a_paused_consumer_cannot_claim_a_gate_that_closed_or_was_replaced`

R-02: `close` never removes a claimed answer without a record. Every claimed answer/claim pair it removes is returned in `CloseReport.claimed` (the gate id and the answer as read) and logged as a `gate_claimed_answer_removed` event carrying that answer, so a consumer that died after its claim and before recording its decision leaves a typed record its caller reports (`resume` prints it as claimed but never applied; that CLI wording and fixture are handed to the stop/recover/status planner, C2) — `gates::tes

R2-05 (round-2 review, codex 3): `close` disposes of the stage's answers before it removes the gate file — unclaimed answers set aside, then each claimed pair's `gate_claimed_answer_removed` event emitted before that pair's two files are removed — and removes the gate file last, so a crash inside `close` leaves the gate file in place with every not-yet-removed pair, which the next `close` (or `resume`'s, 50.1-23) reports again; a crash between a pair's event and its removal reports

R2-04 (round-2 review, codex 5): an answer that was published and whose post-publish re-check then cannot take the gate lock within `GATE_LOCK_WAIT` returns `GateError::PublishedUnconfirmed { phase, stage, observed, waited }`, never `GateLockTimeout`: its message says the answer for that gate id was published and left in place, that whether its gate was still open could not be confirmed, and that its waiter acts on it if the gate is still open; `GateLockTimeout`'s 'nothing was changed' is ret

Gate coordination: the gate-changing operations (`answer`'s pre-publish check and post-publish re-check, `set_aside_unbound`, `claim`, `open_gate`, `close`) hold `.devflow/.gates-NN.lock` (never removed or replaced) only across a few file operations; they acquire it with `try_lock` polled for at most `GATE_LOCK_WAIT` (5 s, below `workflow::WRITE_LOCK_REPAIR_WAIT`) and otherwise return `GateError::GateLockTimeout` having changed nothing — except the post-publish re-check of `answer`/`reap_answer`, whose

D-08 operator ruling (2026-10-26): a bounded gate-lock wait may run while the state write lock is held (50.1-19's `while_owner`, 50.1-21's `clear_state_if`), because gate-lock holders do only file operations and never take the write lock. The two rules that ruling pins are pinned here, where the later of the two constants is defined: the order is always write lock, then gate lock, never the reverse — `gates::tests::gates_never_takes_the_state_write_lock` (a source scan of `gates.rs`, the only modu
V-15 both halves: after the id-less answer is set aside, a valid answer to the live gate id is accepted and read back as bound

V-18 (AR-48-04 path b): a late answer that passed its pre-check while the gate closed and the next gate opened is published under the old id, reported as `GateClosedAfterPublish`, never read as an answer to the next gate, and set aside
D-04 consumption claim: `Gates::claim` publishes the ack exclusively (hard-link); the first claimer gets `Claim::Claimed` and any later one `Claim::AlreadyConsumed`

`Gates::close` sets aside every unconsumed answer for the stage, removes consumed answer/claim pairs (each reported, R-02), the gate file and orphaned durable temps (names ending `.tmp`; a `*.hold-tmp` never matches); `Gates::quarantined` lists every set-aside answer for `status` and `doctor`

Transition rule (until 50.1-15): the unkeyed `write_gate`/`respond`/`reap`/`poll_response*`/`ack`/`cleanup` keep their behaviour (`write_gate` disposes of nothing); `write_gate` additionally writes a gate id; `list_open` reports the id and hides a gate whose live answer or legacy unkeyed answer exists

Quarantine reasons are decided by what the file is, not by when it is set aside: a legacy unkeyed `NN-{stage}.response.json` is always `legacy_unkeyed` (at open, at close and on a waiter's read alike); an unclaimed keyed answer set aside because its gate is no longer live — at `open_gate` or `close` — is `gate_closed`, as is a writer's own publish that landed after its gate closed; a body in a gate's own slot that does not bind to it is `missing_gate_id`, `unparsable` or `other_gate`, whoever

`GateFile` and `OpenGate` gain a field, so the three struct literals outside `gates.rs` (`commands.rs` tests `backdate_gate` and `all_roots_row_includes_gate_with_non_numeric_timestamp`, `tests/gate_sweep_e2e.rs`) are updated in this plan and every workspace target still compiles

prohibitions.statement: A path is never built from a gate id that fails `is_gate_id`; a hostile id in an answer body is quarantined under the literal `noid` (path traversal)

No unconsumed answer is removed by any new function; only an answer whose claim exists is deleted, and every such deletion is reported in `CloseReport.claimed` and a `gate_claimed_answer_removed` event (D-05: never silently deleted; R-02)
`Gates::reap_answer` takes no approval parameter and always writes `approved: false` (T-23-41 kept)

`Gates::set_aside_unbound` and `Gates::answer` never rename, remove or write a file outside the slot of the gate id they were given, and never touch even that slot unless the gate file names that id (R-09)
No gate operation waits for the gate lock longer than `GATE_LOCK_WAIT`, holds it across anything but file operations, or takes the state write lock while holding it
No gate error says nothing was changed after a file was published (R2-04): a published answer whose re-check timed out is `PublishedUnconfirmed`, never `GateLockTimeout`

truths: D-04 registration: a waiter calls `Gates::register_waiter(root, phase, stage, &gate_id)` and holds a `flock` on `NN-{stage}.{gate_id}.waiter` for as long as it waits; `Gates::waiter_status` reads `Live` while it is held and `Absent` once it is released or its process died, so a crashed waiter's registration dies with it
D-04: registration works the same for a foreground waiter with no supervisor socket (preflight gates in `start`, `devflow ship`'s finalization retry)

D-04 order: a waiter opens its gate with `Gates::open_registered(root, phase, stage, context)`, which takes a fresh `GateId`, registers the waiter for it and only then publishes the gate file, so a gate file is never visible before its waiter's registration: a writer that sees it finds the waiter registered, or registered and since dead (`gates::tests::a_writer_answering_the_instant_the_gate_file_appears_finds_its_waiter_registered`, whose in-test publish-then-register control reads `Absent` at the sam

Crash between registering and publishing: no gate file exists, so no writer can learn the id; the registration file is left unheld (`Absent`), listed by nothing (`list_open`, `live_waiter_holders`, `gate_answer_files` skip it) and removed by the stage's next `close`, which reads it `Abandoned` (`gates::tests::a_waiter_killed_between_registering_and_publishing_leaves_no_answerable_gate`, control: killed after publishing leaves a gate whose registration reads `Absent`)

D-05 waiting, R-09: `Gates::await_answer` mutates no file. Each read is `read_answer` of its own gate id: a bound answer returns `Answered`; an answer in its slot that does not bind returns `Unbound { reason }` at once, untouched, so the caller sets it aside through 50.1-06's `Gates::set_aside_unbound` (inside a supervisor, through 50.1-19's owner fence) and waits again; it never reads, moves or removes another gate's files or the legacy unkeyed name (50.1-06's `open_gate`/`close` dispos

R-06 (from 50.1-05's no-replace `Hold::take`): `close` removes a `.waiter` registration only when `liveness::probe` reads it `Abandoned`; a `Live` one (a waiter still waiting, or one mid-take) is never removed by anyone but its owner, through `WaiterRegistration::finish` — `gates::tests::close_removes_only_an_abandoned_waiter_registration`

R-06: a waiter's in-flight take temp (`.NN-{stage}.{gate_id}.waiter.{pid}.{seq}.hold-tmp`, `liveness::HOLD_TEMP_SUFFIX`) in `Gates::dir` does not make `Gates::phases_on_disk` report its phase, and no gate scan reads it as a gate, answer, claim or waiter; a durable `.tmp` still does (it marks a gate write that outlived its phase) — `gates::tests::a_waiter_hold_temp_does_not_make_its_phase_appear_on_disk`

D-13 item 4: `await_answer` reads the answer file only at backoff boundaries (1 s doubling to 60 s) while it checks `cancel` in slices of at most 1 s; `gates::tests::await_answer_backs_off_between_reads_and_still_cancels_within_a_second` fails against today's `poll_response_cancellable`, which reads every second

D-13 item 7 (core half): `await_answer` checks `cancel` before it reads an answer, so a stop accepted in the same second as an answer wins; `gates::tests::await_answer_checks_cancellation_before_reading_an_answer` fails against today's read-first loop

Test-only pre-answer (compiled only under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`): a `NN-{stage}.preanswer.json` present when a gate opens is published as that gate's keyed answer, so tests that answer a gate before it opens keep working without the stale-answer behaviour D-05 removes; in `gates.rs` the gating is enforced by the source scan `gates::tests::the_preanswer_seam_is_compiled_only_in_test_builds` (T-50.1-30), whose planted ungated copy and planted ungated reader each yield exact

Non-reentrancy (plan-check I3): the test-only `consume_preanswer` runs inside `open_gate_as`'s gate-lock critical section and publishes through the unlocked publish step only — it never calls `Gates::answer` or `answer_with_hook`, which would try to take the gate lock a second time from the same process (a second open file description cannot take the `flock` the first holds, so the call would fail with `GateLockTimeout` after `GATE_LOCK_WAIT`), and never takes the state write lock; its doc says so

Transition bridge (deleted in 50.1-15): the unkeyed `poll_response`/`poll_response_cancellable` also read the live gate's keyed answer and share `await_answer`'s backoff and cancel-first loop, still reading only; the unkeyed `cleanup` also removes the stage's keyed answer and claim files, and its waiter files only when they read `Abandoned`

prohibitions.statement: No polling read (`await_answer`, the bridge's two polls) renames, removes or writes any file (R-09)
No `.waiter` file is removed while its probe reads `Live`, except by its owner through `WaiterRegistration::finish` (R-06)

The pre-answer seam and the answer-publish hook have no code path in a release build; no production code writes or reads a `.preanswer.json` name or installs the hook (the pre-answer half in `gates.rs` is also held by `gates::tests::the_preanswer_seam_is_compiled_only_in_test_builds`; the hook half is not scanned)
`waiter_status` never infers a live waiter from a pid, a socket or a plain file's existence; only the held registration lock counts (D-04)

R2-11 (round 2): this race is a defence-in-depth backstop, not a production path — once 50.1-29's R-17 guard (`devflow ship` refuses while a recorded or pending supervisor of the phase is live) and D-17&#

R-08 consumers: `Gates::claim` (50.1-06) publishes only while the gate file still names the claimed id, so a closed or replaced gate is never claimable again; both consumers act on its errors without acting on the answer — `ship_override` refuses on `GateError::NoOpenGate`, `GateError::GateIdMismatch` or `GateError::GateLockTimeout` before `finish_workflow`, consuming nothing; `run_gate_with_timeout` on any `claim` error finishes its registration and returns the error, with no `commit(gate_pending = false)`

R-09 wait arm: `wait_for_gate_response` mutates nothing while it reads; when `Gates::await_answer` (50.1-08) returns `AwaitOutcome::Unbound { reason }` it sets that answer aside through `Gates::set_aside_unbound(.., &gate_id)` (its own gate's slot only, while the gate file still names that id) and waits again with the time left; `NoOpenGate`, `GateIdMismatch` or `GateLockTimeout` from it end the wait with that error, the answer untouched — V-15's CLI test passes as written

D-05 / D-06 stale-answer paths: every `Gates::cleanup` call in the CLI becomes `Gates::close`, which sets unconsumed answers aside instead of deleting them; `start` closes each stage's leftovers and reports what it set aside; a leftover answer `start` could not remove never decides the new run (V-20, `commands::tests::a_leftover_answer_start_could_not_delete_never_decides_the_new_run`)

truths: D-02 / criterion 2 (V-07): while a pending supervisor is live (its liveness lock held, published or not), `devflow status` reports it as a pending launch and names `devflow stop --phase N`, never `devflow resume` — `commands::tests::status_names_stop_not_resume_for_a_live_pending_supervisor`

Criterion 2 negative control (V-08): once that pending supervisor is GONE (lock released), `status` suggests `devflow resume` again — `commands::tests::status_suggests_resume_once_the_pending_supervisor_is_gone`

D-02: `stop` reaches a pending supervisor through its socket exactly as a recorded one; when the pending supervisor is live but has not published yet, `stop` waits (bounded) for its socket and then stops it, or says honestly that nothing was signalled or recorded; when the recorded supervisor is live, stopping it also ends an unpublished successor (Phase 50 safe point 3), so the pending one is addressed after the recorded one is gone

D-02 (V-09): `stop` over an abandoned pending record (lock unheld or file missing) clears it, removes its liveness file, and says what it cleared — `commands::tests::stop_clears_an_abandoned_reservation_and_says_so` (fails today: nothing clears it)

D-11 / criterion 2 (no-fallback arm): the same rig at Code with no fallback writes `cron-instructions-NN.json` whose resume command is `devflow resume --phase N` and emits `rate_limit_resume_scheduled`; no `agent_handoff` event, the agent is unchanged and no successor supervisor launches — `pipeline_launch::tests::a_rate_limit_without_a_fallback_writes_cron_instructions_and_never_hands_off`. R-03 holder record: every acquisition (blocking or bounded) writes `"{pid} {start}\n"` into `.devflow/.state-NN.lock` with `set_len(0)` and one positional `write_all_at(.., 0)` (never through the descriptor's offset, R-01's class rule), and clears it (`set_len(0)`) while still holding the lock just before release, so a non-empty record names the current holder; the record is a diagnostic only — no code signals it. `write_lock_status(root, phase)` is the non-blocking read for `status`/`do

D-08 create path (Pitfall 8): `update_state_with` hands the closure `Existing::{Missing, Unloadable, Loaded}` under the same lock, so a caller can check and create or replace in one step; returning `None` writes nothing

D-03 core half: `update_owned_state(root, phase, launch_id, …)` refuses before the closure runs, writing nothing, with `WorkflowError::NotOwner` unless the state records `launch_id` as `supervisor`; `ownership(state, id)` distinguishes `Recorded`, `PendingOnly` and `Superseded` so the CLI can wait while its id is only pending (D-15)

`clear_state` takes the same write lock, so a removal never interleaves with an update

So no visible `.live`/`.waiter

findings.title: `status` and `doctor` send a `start` killed during preparation to a `resume` that launches an agent with no branch or worktree

A `start` refused during preparation deletes a state file that does not load
999.172's "only a hand edit" is wrong: `stop` can record `stopped` beside a supervisor it did not end, and exit 0
Recovery and the launch guard never ask the recorded supervisor's held liveness file
A persistent read error on an answer slot ends a multi-day gate wait
A pre-authorized answer's waiter abandons its own open gate, and a fenced answer can hold the write lock past the stated bound
The sweep's "fresh gate" test and dry-run unit test pass with the behaviour they name removed
Two e2e tests do not prove the path their names claim
A signal to a foreground `start` parked at a preflight gate records a resumable stop, then deletes the state
`start` and `resume` exit 0, and `start` prints "monitor will auto-advance", when a stop ended the launch before any supervisor ran
A Ship retry after a failed changelog commit writes the changelog entry twice
`abort` reports success when the state could not be removed
The "9 s against 10 s" sum does not model the decision paths; the logged limit is mostly better than recorded
A published answer can be reported as a failed publish
The marker sweep drops directory-entry errors silently
`remove_orphan_hold_temps` does not do what its doc says for a name it cannot parse
`clear_state_if` lacks the guard its sibling has for an untouched project
`HolderError` does not match the crate's error pattern
Stale wording in docs and test comments
A deferred-items entry is out of date
A superseded supervisor still writes shared per-phase files
Comments that disagree with the code
"Never reused" rests on an id that is not guaranteed unique
A close can delete an in-flight publisher's temp
Set-aside answers appear to live forever
Dead shapes
A wedged gate lock in one root ends `gate sweep` for every other root and skips `--reap-strays`
`pending_not_published` can say "nothing was signalled or recorded" after `stop` has already ended the recorded supervisor
`gate approve` can tell the operator to run `resume` or `recover --clean` after its approval was applied
Raw gate ids from the gate file reach the terminal, against the stated rule
Stale wording and a misplaced doc comment
Two `stop_e2e` tests pass without reaching the behaviour their names claim
`resume` sets an answer aside before a launch refusal, and says a rerun will ask again
Safe point 5's comment contradicts the wait it describes
`claim_ship_answer` cites guards that do not exist
A dead in-memory write survives from the old save model
The T-50-68 bound covers one stop path out of several
`decimal_phase_paths` says it covers every derived path, and misses this phase's new ones
The SIGKILL leak test hand-clears the record, so it never runs `resume` over a real one
`devflow parallel` arms `devflow.toml`'s `fallback_agent`, contradicting its comment, and its refusal names a flag `parallel` lacks
The never-silent gate after a canary-refused failover offers retry and loop options that end the run with no gate (999.187, made reachable by this phase)
The failover guard also covers `run_preflight`'s own gate and the relaunch its answer starts, contrary to its doc comments
The `devflow.toml` key parses agent names more strictly than the `--fallback-agent` flag
An unparseable `devflow.toml` is now reported as a `fallback_agent` problem even when the file has no such key
The torn-final-line clause claims "a quota denial cannot be ruled out" for agents whose denials the classifier cannot detect at all
